key_insight: The paper introduces Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI) as a new inverse-problem paradigm that solves problems by exploiting intrinsic mathematical or physical structure instead of iterative objective minimization.
engineering_relevance: SDI could improve efficiency, interpretability, and parameter decoupling in scientific computing, with potential impact on inverse problems in PDEs, imaging, and physics-informed machine learning.
method: MSDI: derive a pseudo-inverse from spectral/unitary diagonalization structure.
PSDI: use physical structure via virtual-source projection for waveform inversion imaging.
PSDI: use structural projections inspired by physical-system analogies for back-propagation in neural networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and programmatic; it presents a taxonomy and representative methods but does not report experimental benchmarks or numerical evaluation.
watch_item: The framework is still an emerging paradigm, so practical performance, generality, and computational cost will need validation on concrete inverse-problem benchmarks.
paper_title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm for Solving Inverse Problems
